caption: where does he take them 🛶
logline: A villager kid says a player took thirty-nine villagers in his boat and none came back, so today she got in herself to find out where; he took her Mom and her uncle, and the first time he came he stared at the old empty village across the water where a light was on in one window; at dusk her boat bumps that village and Mom, her uncle and the lady from the window are waiting, every house full.
question: why has this player taken thirty-nine villagers in his boat, and where did they go?
premise: A player took thirty-nine villagers in his boat, one at a time, and none came back. Today the kid gets in herself to find out where: number forty. He took her Mom last week and her uncle before. The first time he came, he stared across the water at the old empty village, where a light was on in one window, and said someone's been alone a long time.
twist: Every Minecraft player knows a villager dragged in a boat is going to a trading hall. He isn't building one. He is filling Fernbank, the empty village across the inlet where the old librarian has lived alone with the golem for years, one villager at a time: number forty is the fortieth neighbour he has brought her. At dusk the boat bumps the dock, every window is lit, and Mom and the uncle are waiting at the dock's foot beside the librarian. 'None of them came back. They must love it there' was true.
payoff_note: the cut to S11 lands on EMPTY (L07's last word: the picture contradicts the word); L08 says the reveal over S11 (story_format beat 6); L09, the one beat, echoes L01; S11 holds 1.0 s after L09; the Short ends there.

A man (a player, nameless) first came about day 5700; the kid followed him down to the water, where he looked across at Fernbank's one lit window. lines.text: A man is / KIDNAPPING / my VILLAGE. / In a BOAT. / On the GRASS.
lines.say: A man is KIDNAPPING my village. In a BOAT. On the GRASS.
lines.direction: bright and quick, telling a friend a real mystery; straight into KIDNAPPING with no lead-in pause; no beats, the fragments clipped and quick; never scared
lines.note: hook (STANDARDS 0v, owner 2026-11-12 "make our hooks absurd"; 0t, hook frame study 2026-11-12): said flat, as plain fact, the narrator believes it; no stock why tag. 0t: the key word KIDNAPPING (the title's CAPS word) is word 4, about 1.3-1.7 s at Pip's pace (~3 words/s); the first sentence is done by ~2.1 s, the whole line by ~3.4 s. S01 holds on the kid's face in the moving boat until KIDNAPPING ends; the cut to S01b lands on VILLAGE. Tightened from 'A man is kidnapping my whole VILLAGE. One at a TIME. In a BOAT. On the GRASS.' (the study's line; 'whole' and 'One at a TIME' cut, L02's 'number FORTY' carries the one-at-a-time count). 'Kidnapping' is her word; L09 turns it ('I'm not going back either')

lines.text: Today, / I got in MYSELF. / I'm number FORTY.
lines.say: Today, I got in myself. I'm number forty.
lines.direction: proud of her own plan, a little giggle on FORTY
lines.note: beat 3 and 5: the narrator is the one who wants to know and goes to look (vanilla: a mob that walks into a boat gets in). Two-way clue 1: 'number forty' (a hall's stock count / the fortieth neighbour); the man glances back on FORTY r6 opening (critic 0t): 'So' cut (the study's line 2) so S02 ends ~5.6 s and Mom/Uncle land a new face every ~1.2 s.

lines.text: He took MOM / last WEEK. / And my UNCLE. / They must LOVE it there.
lines.say: He took Mom last week. And my uncle. They must love it there.
lines.direction: bright, a fun fact, no worry at all; LOVE sure and sweet
lines.note: beat 4 (someone loved at stake) and two-way clue 2: 'They must LOVE it there' (0a; a player reads cells, and it is literally true). S07 on MOM, S07b on UNCLE, S08 (the look back at the two shut doors) on LOVE

lines.text: The FIRST time he came, / he stared across the WATER / at the old EMPTY village. / Somebody left a light on / in ONE WINDOW.
lines.say: The first time he came, he stared across the water at the old empty village. Somebody left a light on in one window.
lines.direction: storytelling, bright, the last bit a shrug of a fact
lines.note: two-way clue 3, a flashback (graded): 'Somebody left a light on in ONE WINDOW' is the kid's misreading of the lit window (0a) and plants WINDOW for L08's 'the lady from the WINDOW' (critic r3 must-fix 2); S04 on most of the line, the cut to S04b's long lens on WINDOW (the old librarian alone at her lit west window)

lines.text: Someone's been ALONE / a long TIME.
lines.say: Someone's been alone a long time.
lines.direction: plain, normal volume, to himself, looking away across the water
lines.note: the man's one line, on screen while he says it; plain, never low and tender (the out-of-context read). Two-way clue 4 with L06

lines.text: I think / he means HIMSELF. / He doesn't have / any FRIENDS.
lines.say: I think he means himself. He doesn't have any friends.
lines.direction: bright and SURE of it, sweet, a little sorry for him (critic r3 watch item: this misread must pull the guess away from the window)
lines.note: 0a: the kid's misreading of 'someone' (it is the lady in the window)

lines.text: We crossed the WATER, / and when it got DARK, / we bumped into / the old EMPTY village.
lines.say: We crossed the water, and when it got dark, we bumped into the old empty village.
lines.direction: giggling at the crossing, then a little slower on the last words, curious
lines.note: beat 5 (she goes to look). S09 on WATER (he rows his own boat and tows hers on the lead: she sat in first, so a player can't steer hers), S10 on 'bumped' (the bow knocks the dock post), the cut to S11 lands on EMPTY: the picture contradicts the word, the next line says it

lines.text: MOM was there, / and my UNCLE, / and the lady from the WINDOW, / and every house was FULL.
lines.say: Mom was there, and my uncle, and the lady from the window, and every house was full.
lines.direction: wonder, a delighted rush, the last word FULL landing big
lines.note: beat 6, the reveal SAID in one plain sentence: the kid names what she sees (Mom, Uncle, the lady from the window, every house full); the viewer makes the one jump (he was filling the lonely lady's empty village). Over S11

lines.text: None of them came BACK. / I'm not going back EITHER.
lines.say: None of them came back. I'm not going back either.
lines.direction: happy, settled, quick; the last word bright
lines.note: beat 7, the one beat after the reveal: turns L01's 'KIDNAPPING' into 'not going back either' and turns it (they stayed because they wanted to); cut 1.0 s after. Critic r3 should-fix 1 (why didn't Mom come back to say?) answered in the picture: villagers can't row, and no boat waits at Fernbank's dock but the two that just came in
